title_en: Cao Zhongquan v. Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office and Shanghai Jingkai Service Machinery Co., Ltd. — administrative dispute over invalidation of utility model patent
ruling_gist_en: 1. The technical field is the specific technical field to which the claimed invention or utility model pertains or is applied, and it is neither a broader or adjacent technical field, nor the invention or utility model itself. The technical field to which an invention or utility model belongs shall be determined based on the content defined in the claims, and generally determined by the subject matter name of the patent, in combination with the technical functions and uses achieved by the technical solution.
keywords_en: administrative; administrative dispute over patent invalidation; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Beijing; Shanghai; Zhejiang Province; natural person; state organ; legal person; Patent Law; determination of technical field; whether to order a new decision after revocation of a specific administrative act; judicial review of the Patent Reexamination Board's invalidation decision; reversal of judgment; invalidation of utility model patent right; examination decision of the Patent Reexamination Board; oil retention device for the knife sharpening mechanism of a cutting machine; unification of adjudication standards; clarification of judicial benchmarks; patent right; application for retrial; intellectual property; administrative dispute over invalidation of utility model patent
full_text_en:
曹忠泉 v. 国家知识产权局专利复审委员会、上海精凯服务机械有限公司 — 实用新型专利权无效行政纠纷案

【Ruling Summary】

I. The technical field is the specific technical field to which the claimed invention or utility model belongs or is applied. It is neither a broader or neighboring technical field, nor the invention or utility model itself. The technical field to which an invention or utility model belongs shall be determined based on the content defined in the claims, generally according to the subject name of the patent, taking into account the technical functions and uses achieved by the technical solution.

II. When a people's court decides in a judgment to revoke or partially revoke a specific administrative act under review, it may order the defendant to make a new specific administrative act. However, whether to order the defendant to make a new specific administrative act shall depend on the specific circumstances of the case.

III. When a people's court reviews a decision of the Patent Reexamination Board (PRB) on an invalidation request, in a situation where the PRB considers the patent right valid but the people's court considers it invalid, the court shall, when revoking the challenged decision, also order the PRB to make a new decision. In a situation where the PRB considers the patent right invalid, the court shall distinguish between two scenarios when deciding whether to order the PRB to make a new decision: if the PRB has fully evaluated all invalidity grounds and evidence raised by the requester, and the people's court considers the patent valid, the court need not order the PRB to make a new decision; if the PRB has not fully evaluated all invalidity grounds and evidence raised by the requester and the invalidity decision based on partial grounds and corresponding evidence cannot be sustained, the people's court shall also order the PRB to make a new decision evaluating the other invalidity grounds and evidence raised by the requester.

Administrative Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2012) Xing Ti Zi No. 7

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Cao Zhongquan, male, Han ethnicity, born in 1951, General Manager of Zhejiang Dayang Yiche Co., Ltd., residing in Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province.

Agent ad litem: Cai Zhengbao, male, Han ethnicity, born in 1951, patent agent of Taizhou Fangyuan Patent Agency, residing in Linhai City, Zhejiang Province.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office. Address: Floors 10-12, Yingu Building, No. 9, West Fourth Ring North Road, Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zhang Maoyu, Deputy Director of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Xing Wenfei, Examiner of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Mao Jin, Examiner of the Board.

Third Party at First Instance: Shanghai Jingkai Garment Machinery Co., Ltd. Address: No. 185, Moyu Road, Anting Town, Jiading District, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Ruan Jianguang, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Ye Wandong, male, Han ethnicity, born in 1973, patent agent of Beijing Gongxin United Intellectual Property Agency, residing in Chaoyang District, Beijing.

The applicant for retrial, Cao Zhongquan, dissatisfied with the administrative judgment (2010) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 634 of the Beijing High People's Court in the dispute over the invalidation of a utility model patent right against the respondent, the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office (hereinafter the "Patent Reexamination Board") and the third party at first instance, Shanghai Jingkai Garment Machinery Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Jingkai Company"), applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered an administrative ruling on December 21, 2011, (2011) Zhi Xing Zi No. 18, granting the retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a public hearing on March 5, 2012. Cai Zhengbao, agent ad litem of Cao Zhongquan; Xing Wenfei and Mao Jin, agents ad litem of the Patent Reexamination Board; and Ye Wandong, agent ad litem of Jingkai Company, appeared before the court. The trial of this case is now concluded.

The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court found after trial: This patent is a utility model patent titled "Oil Retention Device for Helical Gear Set in Cutting Machine Sharpening Mechanism" published by the State Intellectual Property Office on October 4, 2006, with patent number 200520014575.5, application date September 1, 2005, and the patentee is Cao Zhongquan. The claims are: "1. An oil retention device for a helical gear set in a cutting machine sharpening mechanism, characterized in that oil retaining walls (4) are provided around the helical gear position (2) and the intermediate gear position (3). 2. The oil retention device according to claim 1, characterized in that a notch is left on the wall (4) for the intermediate gear inside to engage with a transmission gear outside. 3. The oil retention device according to claim 2, characterized in that the wall (4) is integrally formed with the helical gear housing (8) or the sharpening mechanism housing (1). 4. The oil retention device according to claim 1, characterized in that an arc-shaped cover plate (7) is provided at the transmission gear position (5) outside the wall (6)."

Jingkai Company filed a request for invalidation of this patent on November 27, 2008, and submitted Attachments 1 and 2 as evidence. The Patent Reexamination Board accepted the above invalidation request and issued a notice of acceptance of the invalidation request to Cao Zhongquan and Jingkai Company on November 27, 2008, simultaneously forwarding copies of the invalidation request and the attachments listed in the attachment list submitted by Jingkai Company to Cao Zhongquan, requiring him to submit observations within a specified period. Cao Zhongquan submitted a statement of observations on December 19, 2008. Jingkai Company submitted a statement of observations and Attachments 4-1 to 5-9 as evidence on December 26, 2008, among which Attachment 5-1 is a copy of the specification of US Patent No. 3672586, 8 pages, and a Chinese translation of 7 pages, with a publication date of June 27, 1972. Jingkai Company argued that from Figures 3, 5, and 6 of Attachment 5-1, it can be clearly seen that 200B, 200, and 200C constitute oil retaining walls, enclosing the three gears, with the notch formed between the top point of 200B and the top point of 200C corresponding to the notch in this patent, allowing the gear to connect with the transmission screw. Walls 202B and 212 together cover the transmission screw 144 to prevent oil from splashing. Gear 146 corresponds to the "intermediate gear" in this patent, gear 160 corresponds to the "helical gear", and the front part 200A, cylindrical part 200B, and rear arc part 200C of the guard 200 together constitute the "oil retaining wall" in this patent, used to prevent lubricating oil absorbed from the oil groove 162 from splashing. The space between the top of the rear arc part 200C and the top of the cylindrical part 200B constitutes the "notch" in this patent, used to provide the meshing connection between the gear and the screw. Providing an arc-shaped cover around the screw 144 to prevent oil from being thrown off as the screw rotates is common general knowledge. Therefore, Attachment 5-1 negates the novelty and inventiveness of claims 1, 2, and 4 of this patent. The Patent Reexamination Board received another statement of observations from Jingkai Company on December 29, 2008. Cao Zhongquan submitted a power of attorney, a statement of observations, and a replacement sheet for the amended claims to the Patent Reexamination Board on January 4, 2009. The specific amendment method was: deleting claim 1 from the published text, elevating claim 2 from the published text to become new claim 1, and using the limiting parts of claims 3 and 4 from the published text as the limiting parts of dependent claims 2 and 3 that further limit the new independent claim 1. The Patent Reexamination Board issued a notice of forwarding documents on January 12, 2009, forwarding the statements of observations and attachments submitted by Cao Zhongquan on December 19, 2008, and January 4, 2009, to Jingkai Company, and forwarding the statements of observations and attachments submitted by Jingkai Company on December 26, 2008, and December 29, 2008, to Cao Zhongquan. Jingkai Company submitted another statement of observations and Attachments 6 and 7 as evidence on February 9, 2009, clearly stating that because Cao Zhongquan had merged claims 1 and 2, it was adding additional grounds and evidence Attachments 6 and 7. The Patent Reexamination Board issued a notice of forwarding documents on February 16, 2009, forwarding the statement of observations and attachments submitted by Cao Zhongquan on February 6, 2009, to Jingkai Company, and forwarding the statement of observations and attachments submitted by Jingkai Company on February 9, 2009, to Cao Zhongquan.

The Patent Reexamination Board conducted an oral hearing on February 25, 2009. Jingkai Company had no objection to the amendments made by Cao Zhongquan to the claims. The oral hearing was conducted on the basis of the amended text submitted by Cao Zhongquan on January 4, 2009. Jingkai Company submitted originals of Attachments 4-1 to 4-15 and 5-1 to 5-9 at the hearing. Cao Zhongquan had no objection to the authenticity of Attachments 4 and 5 and no objection to the accuracy of the translations. Jingkai Company explicitly abandoned Attachments 1 and 2 as evidence and clarified the specific grounds for invalidation. Cao Zhongquan submitted a statement of observations and one page of amended claims on February 27, 2009. Upon verification, the amendment method of the claims was consistent with the method stated orally at the hearing. The content of the amended claims is: "1. An oil retention device for a helical gear set in a cutting machine sharpening mechanism, characterized in that oil retaining walls (4) are provided around the helical gear position (2) and the intermediate gear position (3), and a notch is left on the wall (4) for the intermediate gear inside to engage with a transmission gear outside. 2. The oil retention device according to claim 1, characterized in that the wall (4) is integrally formed with the helical gear housing (8) or the sharpening mechanism housing (1). 3. The oil retention device according to claim 1, characterized in that an arc-shaped cover plate (7) is provided at the transmission gear position (5) outside the wall (4)."

On April 14, 2009, the Patent Reexamination Board issued Decision No. 13216 on the Invalidation Request (hereinafter "Decision No. 13216"), declaring all claims of this patent invalid. The decision held that Attachment 5-1 was published before the application date of this patent, and Cao Zhongquan had no objection to the authenticity of the attachment or the accuracy of its Chinese translation, so Attachment 5-1 could be used as prior art to assess the novelty or inventiveness of the claims of this patent. Claim 1 of this patent sought to protect an oil retention device for a helical gear set in a cutting machine sharpening mechanism, comprising the following technical features: (1) oil retaining walls (4) are provided around the helical gear position (2) and the intermediate gear position (3); (2) a notch is left on the wall (4) for the intermediate gear inside to engage with a transmission gear outside. Attachment 5-1 discloses a gear lubrication part in a winding machine, specifically disclosing the following technical content: The thrower ring 160 is driven by matching with gear 146, and is enclosed by a guard 200 (Figures 3 to 6), which delimits the lubricant obtained from the oil sump 162 and reflects the lubricant rotatably spraying gears 146 and 150, thereby moving upward. More particularly, the guard 200 is suitably and tightly fixed to the base support 198 (Figure 4), and extends directly forward portion 200A into the oil sump 162 along the thrower ring 160, which has a cylindrical member 200B extending upward from member 200A, and spaced apart from gear 150. The guard 200 also has a generally cylindrical rear arc piece 200C, extendable outward from the thrower ring 160, and close to the gap of gear 146. The thrower ring 160, gears 146 and 150, and the guard 200 provide operating means to obtain lubricant from the source provided by the oil sump 162 and to eject the lubricant in a spray state or inject the thrower ring or spray the lubricant through the first delivery tube 202 (see Attachment 5-1 Chinese translation, page 6, paragraph 2, and Figures 3 to 6). In Attachment 5-1, the front part 200A, cylindrical part 200B, and rear arc part 200C of the guard 200 together enclose the gear set inside, preventing the lubricating oil on the gears from splashing, corresponding to the "oil retaining wall" in claim 1; gear 146 corresponds to the "intermediate gear" in claim 1; gear 160 corresponds to the "helical gear" in claim 1; there is an opening between the top point of cylindrical part 200B and the top point of rear arc part 200C, thereby allowing the gear and the thread to connect. From the translation and drawings of Attachment 5-1, it can be determined that the above thread is a thread on a screw, and this opening corresponds to the "notch" in claim 1. The differences between the technical solution of claim 1 of this patent and Attachment 5-1 are: (1) the technical solution of claim 1 of this patent is directed to a cutting machine sharpening mechanism, while the application environment of the technical solution of Attachment 5-1 is a winding machine; (2) the intermediate gear in this patent engages with an external transmission gear, while gear 146 in Attachment 5-1 cooperates with a transmission screw having threads. Worm gear transmission, spur gear transmission, helical gear transmission, bevel gear transmission, etc., are all commonly used technical means in the relevant technical field. Cutting machine sharpening mechanisms and winding machines are both mechanical devices, both involving the problem of gear set oil retention and lubrication. According to actual needs, replacing the screw transmission in Attachment 5-1 with helical gear transmission and applying the gear set oil retention and lubrication technology from the winding machine to the cutting machine sharpening mechanism to obtain the technical solution of claim 1 is easily conceivable and achievable for a person skilled in the art. Therefore, claim 1 lacks substantive features and progress relative to Attachment 5-1, and does not comply with Article 22, paragraph 3 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China as amended in 2000 (hereinafter "Patent Law").

The additional technical feature of claim 2 of this patent specifically limits that the wall (4) is integrally formed with the helical gear housing (8) or the sharpening mechanism housing (1). Attachment 5-1 already discloses the technical content of suitably and tightly fixing the guard 200 to the base support 198, i.e., it gives the inspiration to fix the guard corresponding to the wall to the support. The technology of integral forming belongs to common general knowledge in the relevant technical field. Combining the above common general knowledge in the relevant technical field to integrally form the wall (4) with the helical gear housing (8) or the sharpening mechanism housing (1) to obtain the technical solution of claim 2 is obvious to a person skilled in the art. The technical solution of claim 2 lacks substantive features and progress relative to Attachment 5-1, and does not comply with Article 22, paragraph 3 of the Patent Law.

The additional technical feature of claim 3 of this patent further limits that an arc-shaped cover plate is provided at the transmission gear position outside the wall. Attachment 5-1 also discloses the following technical content: Since the lubricant passes upward through the first delivery tube 202, through the access opening 204 (Figure 4) in the baffle 206, which forms the bottom wall of the receiving portion 208 of the second or bottom delivery tube 210. Inside the second delivery tube 210, the lubricant drips onto the baffle 206, which descends to the front side wall 202A and moves toward the first passage 214 between the baffles. The passage 214 also descends to the front side wall 202A. By welding, the baffle and the passage are fixed to the top wall 212 in any reasonable manner (see Attachment 5-1 Chinese translation, page 6, paragraph 3, and Figures 3 to 6). The baffle 206 in Attachment 5-1 is located above the gear set and the threaded screw, and cooperates with the front part 200A, cylindrical part 200B, and rear arc part 200C of the guard 200 (which correspond to the "oil retaining wall") to objectively keep the lubricating oil around the gears. The main function of the arc-shaped cover plate in claim 3 is to cooperate with the wall to retain the splashing lubricating oil around the helical gear. Therefore, the baffle 206 in Attachment 5-1 corresponds to the arc-shaped cover plate in claim 3. Thus, Attachment 5-1 already discloses the additional technical feature of claim 3. In the case where the claim it depends on lacks inventiveness relative to Attachment 5-1, the technical solution of claim 3 lacks substantive features and progress relative to Attachment 5-1, and does not comply with Article 22, paragraph 3 of the Patent Law. The Patent Reexamination Board made no evaluation of the other invalidity grounds raised by Jingkai Company.

Cao Zhongquan, dissatisfied with Decision No. 13216, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, requesting revocation of the decision.

Beijing No.1 Intermediate People's Court held that: This patent and Document 5-1 are both mechanical devices, both relating to the oil retention and lubrication of gear sets, and therefore belong to the same or similar technical field. During the oral hearing before the Patent Reexamination Board, Cao Zhongquan indicated that he had no objection to the authenticity of Document 5-1 and the accuracy of its Chinese translation. The Patent Reexamination Board's use of the patent specification of Document 5-1 and its Chinese translation as prior art for evaluating the inventiveness of this patent was proper. The technical solution of claim 1 of this patent does not specifically define the shape and structure of the oil-retaining wall; its main function is to retain lubricating oil around the gear set, ensuring good lubrication for the helical gear set, reducing noise and wear, while also specifying that there is an opening in the wall. In Document 5-1, the directly forward portion 200A, cylindrical portion 200B, and rear arc piece 200C of the shield 200 collectively enclose the gear set inside, and their function is also to prevent splashing of lubricating oil obtained from the oil tank, retaining the oil around the gear set, and also providing inlet and outlet channels for the lubricating oil. Therefore, the shield 200 in Document 5-1 is equivalent to the "oil-retaining wall" in claim 1 of this patent; the gear 146 in Document 5-1 is equivalent to the "intermediate gear" inside the "oil-retaining wall" in claim 1; the gear 160 is equivalent to the "helical gear" inside the "oil-retaining wall" in claim 1. According to the description of claim 1, the opening functions to provide space for the intermediate gear to engage with the transmission gear; the opening between the top vertex of the cylindrical portion 200B and the top vertex of the rear arc piece 200C in Document 5-1 allows the gear to connect with the thread on the screw, thereby also achieving a connecting function, which is equivalent to the opening in claim 1. The main difference between the technical solution of claim 1 and Document 5-1 is that the former is for a cutting machine's knife sharpening mechanism, while the latter is applied in a winding machine; in the former, the intermediate gear engages with an external transmission gear, while in the latter, gear 146 cooperates with a threaded transmission screw. Substituting a gear for the screw in Document 5-1 in terms of transmission method, and applying the oil retention and lubrication technology for gear sets in a winding machine to the knife sharpening mechanism of a cutting machine, the technical solution of claim 1 is easily conceivable and achievable for a person skilled in the art. Therefore, claim 1 does not possess inventiveness. The baffle 206 in Document 5-1 is located above the gear set and the threaded screw, and cooperates with the directly forward portion 200A, cylindrical portion 200B, and rear arc piece 200C of the shield 200 (equivalent to the "oil-retaining wall"), objectively achieving the effect of retaining lubricating oil around the gear. The main function of the arc cover plate in claim 3 of this patent is also to cooperate with the wall to retain splashed lubricating oil around the helical gear. Therefore, the baffle 206 in Document 5-1 is equivalent to the arc cover plate of claim 3. When claim 1 lacks inventiveness relative to Document 5-1, the technical solution of claim 3 does not have substantive features and progress relative to Document 5-1. Although Cao Zhongquan argued that the commercial success of this patent indirectly proves its inventiveness, since he did not submit corresponding evidence, his argument is not supported. Furthermore, Cao Zhongquan has already admitted that if claim 1 lacks inventiveness, claim 2, as a dependent claim, also lacks inventiveness. In summary, Decision No. 13216 made by the Patent Reexamination Board found clear facts, applied the law correctly, and followed proper procedures. The court of first instance accordingly rendered Administrative Judgment (2009) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 1326, upholding Decision No. 13216. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 100 was borne by Cao Zhongquan.

Cao Zhongquan, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Beijing High People's Court, requesting revocation of the first-instance judgment and the Patent Reexamination Board's Decision No. 13216.

Upon review, the Beijing High People's Court found that, in the first instance, Cao Zhongquan did not raise any objection to the finding in Decision No. 13216 that amended claim 2 lacked inventiveness.

The Beijing High People's Court held: If a petitioner adds grounds for invalidation after one month from the date of filing the invalidation request, the Patent Reexamination Board generally will not consider it; however, if the patentee amends the claims by way of consolidation, the petitioner may add invalidation grounds and provide specific explanations within a period specified by the Patent Reexamination Board. Cao Zhongquan amended the claims by consolidation during the invalidation proceeding, and Jingkai Company proposed to use Document 5-1 to evaluate the inventiveness of amended claim 2, which was an invalidation ground added within the period specified by the Patent Reexamination Board. Moreover, during the oral hearing, Cao Zhongquan fully stated his opinions on this invalidation ground and indicated that he would not supplement any written opinions. Therefore, the Patent Reexamination Board fully protected the rights of both the patentee and the petitioner in both procedural and substantive aspects, and there was no illegality. Although this patent and Document 5-1 are applied in different mechanical devices, both relate to the oil retention and lubrication of gear sets in mechanical equipment and belong to the same technical field. The Patent Reexamination Board and the court of first instance correctly found that the shield 200 in Document 5-1 is equivalent to the "oil-retaining wall" in claim 1 of this patent. Gear 146 in Document 5-1 is equivalent to the "intermediate gear" inside the "oil-retaining wall" in claim 1; gear 160 is equivalent to the "helical gear" inside the "oil-retaining wall" in claim 1; the opening between the top vertex of the cylindrical portion 200B and the top vertex of the rear arc piece 200C in Document 5-1 is equivalent to the opening in claim 1. The technical solution of claim 1 differs from Document 5-1 in terms of gear transmission method, but both transmission methods are conventional technical means in the relevant technical field. Therefore, applying the oil retention and lubrication technology for gear sets in the winding machine of Document 5-1 to the knife sharpening mechanism of a cutting machine to obtain the technical solution of claim 1 is easily conceivable for a person skilled in the art. Claim 1 lacks inventiveness relative to Document 5-1. Claim 2 further defines that the wall (4) is integrally formed with the helical gear brake (8) or the knife sharpening brake (1). Document 5-1 discloses that the shield 200 is suitably and rigidly fixed to the base support 198, providing a technical teaching to fix the shield (equivalent to the wall) to the support. The integral formation technique is common general knowledge in the art, and a person skilled in the art could easily combine the two to arrive at the technical solution of claim 2. Therefore, based on the lack of inventiveness of claim 1, claim 2 also lacks inventiveness. Claim 3 further defines that an arc cover plate is provided at the transmission gear outside the wall, the main function of which is to cooperate with the wall to retain splashed lubricating oil around the helical gear. The baffle 206 in Document 5-1 is located above the gear set and the threaded screw, and cooperates with the shield 200 (equivalent to the "oil-retaining wall") to also achieve the effect of retaining lubricating oil around the gear. Therefore, Document 5-1 has already disclosed the additional technical features of claim 3. Based on the lack of inventiveness of claim 1, claim 3 also lacks inventiveness. In summary, Cao Zhongquan's grounds of appeal lack factual and legal basis. The first-instance judgment found clear facts and applied the law correctly. Accordingly, the court rendered the judgment: dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment. The first-instance and second-instance case acceptance fees of RMB 100 each were borne by Cao Zhongquan.

Cao Zhongquan applied for retrial, arguing: 1. On February 25, 2009, during the oral hearing, Jingkai Company submitted a statement of opinion and declared the withdrawal of the statement of opinion sent on February 9, 2009. Document 5-1 and others, as an integral part of the February 9 statement of opinion, should be deemed withdrawn accordingly. As a result, Document 5-1 should be considered as submitted on the day of the oral hearing, which exceeded the statutory evidentiary period. 2. The translation of Document 5-1 submitted by Jingkai Company on December 29, 2008, had 12 pages, but the Patent Reexamination Board used a modified 7-page translation. This translation contained multiple revisions, especially changing the original translation "shield 200 also has a universal cylindrical rear quadrant 200C" to "shield 200 also has a universal cylindrical rear arc piece 200C". This translation is inaccurate, yet it was adopted in Decision No. 13216 and the judgments of first and second instance. 3. The Guidelines for Examination require that for a technical teaching to exist in the inventive step assessment, the technical means disclosed in the cited document must have the same function as the distinguishing feature; otherwise, it cannot be considered a technical teaching. The characterizing part of claim 1 of this patent is "an oil-retaining wall (4) is provided around the helical gear position (2) and the intermediate gear position (3)", which functions to retain lubricating oil around the helical gear set and prevent contamination of the fabric being cut. Document 5-1 has a shield 200 that is open at the top and bottom, spraying lubricating oil from the bottom oil box 162 to above the shield 200, which functions to "deliver" rather than retain the oil inside the shield 200. Therefore, the functions are opposite. The characterizing part of amended claim 3 is "an arc cover plate (7) is provided at the transmission gear position (5) outside the wall (6)", which functions to directly retain lubricating oil around the transmission gear; the baffle 206 in Document 5-1 functions to receive lubricating oil sprayed from bottom to top and deliver it to other parts requiring lubrication, i.e., a "receiving" function. Their functions are also opposite, so it cannot be found that there is a technical teaching. The two distinguishing features identified by the Patent Reexamination Board in Decision No. 13216 between this patent and Document 5-1 are erroneous; these distinguishing features were neither mentioned nor heard in the invalidation proceeding. The distinguishing feature closely related to the technical problem solved by this patent and Document 5-1 is that claim 1 has a "wall" surrounding the gear set, while Document 5-1 has "shields 200A, 200B and 200C" arranged on both sides of the gear set. Decision No. 13216 found that "both relate to the oil retention and lubrication of gear sets" and "the effect of retaining lubricating oil around the gear set is equivalent to the oil-retaining wall in claim 1", which is clearly inconsistent with the facts. The "shield 200" in Document 5-1 differs from the "wall" of this patent, and the "baffle 206" also differs from the "arc cover plate" of this patent. The international classification of Document 5-1 is B65H, while the international classifications of this patent are D06H and F16N; they are clearly not similar or related technical fields. However, the Patent Reexamination Board, disregarding whether there is a technical teaching, merely emphasized that "both are mechanical devices" and made the finding, which obviously violates the relevant provisions of the Guidelines for Examination and the legislative intent of Paragraph 3 of Article 22 of the Patent Law that the inventiveness standard for utility model patents should be lower than that for invention patents. In summary, Cao Zhongquan requested revocation of the first-instance and second-instance judgments and Decision No. 13216.

The respondent, the Patent Reexamination Board, argued: Cao Zhongquan raised no objection to the authenticity of Document 5-1 or the accuracy of its Chinese translation; therefore, this document can be used as prior art for evaluating the novelty or inventiveness of the claims of this patent. A comparison of claim 1 with Document 5-1 shows that claim 1 lacks substantive features and progress relative to Document 5-1, failing to comply with Paragraph 3 of Article 22 of the Patent Law. The findings in Decision No. 13216 regarding the "oil-retaining wall" and "arc cover plate" are objective. Although the classification numbers of this patent and Document 5-1 differ, both are mechanical devices and both relate to the oil retention and lubrication of gear sets; the technical problems solved are the same, so they belong to the same technical field. The Patent Reexamination Board does not concur with the issues raised by Cao Zhongquan in his retrial application and maintains the views expressed in Decision No. 13216.

The third party in the first instance, Jingkai Company, stated that its evidence was not submitted beyond the prescribed period and agreed with the Patent Reexamination Board's reply.

Upon retrial, this court finds: The facts found by the first-instance and second-instance courts are true. Additionally, the court finds that on December 26, 2008, Jingkai Company submitted a statement of opinion and evidence including Document 5-1. In its statement of opinion dated February 9, 2009, Jingkai Company explicitly used the previously submitted Document 5-1 as a cited document. During the oral hearing on February 25, 2009, Jingkai Company submitted a statement of opinion on the spot, in which it declared the withdrawal of its statement of opinion submitted on February 9, 2009, but did not withdraw Document 5-1. The oral hearing record submitted by the Patent Reexamination Board indicates that during the oral hearing, Cao Zhongquan's remarks mentioned the relevant content in the sixth line of the second-to-last paragraph on page 6 of the Chinese translation of Document 5-1, which is consistent with the 7-page Chinese translation of Document 5-1.

The specification of this patent states in the "Summary of the Invention": "The utility model provides a wall surrounding the helical gear set to retain splashed lubricating oil around the helical gear, ensuring good lubrication of the helical gear set, significantly reducing sharpening noise, while also reducing energy consumption, prolonging the service life of the helical gear, and preventing contamination of the fabric being cut." In the "Detailed Description", it states: "To prevent the transmission rod gear from throwing out the lubricating oil inside the wall, an arc cover plate 7 is provided above the gear position 5."

This court holds in retrial: The issues in dispute in this case are whether Jingkai Company's submission of Document 5-1 exceeded the statutory evidentiary period; the issue regarding the submission of the translation of Document 5-1; and whether this patent possesses inventiveness compared to Document 5-1. The analysis is as follows:

(1) Whether Jingkai Company's submission of Document 5-1 exceeded the statutory evidentiary period

Pursuant to Article 66 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2002) (hereinafter referred to as the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law), after the Patent Reexamination Board accepts a request for invalidation, the petitioner may add grounds or supplement evidence within one month from the date of filing the invalidation request. If grounds are added or evidence is supplemented beyond that period, the Patent Reexamination Board may disregard them. In this case, Jingkai Company supplemented and submitted Document 5-1 within one month after the Patent Reexamination Board accepted the invalidation request, which complies with the law. Although Jingkai Company, in the statement of opinion submitted during the oral hearing, declared the withdrawal of its statement of opinion dated February 9, 2009, this declaration only indicated the withdrawal of the relevant opinion, and does not mean that Document 5-1, as the cited document in that opinion, was also withdrawn. Nor was it necessary for Jingkai Company to withdraw and resubmit Document 5-1 during the oral hearing. Moreover, Jingkai Company had consistently used Document 5-1 as a cited document, and Cao Zhongquan had made multiple statements regarding this cited document. Therefore, Cao Zhongquan's claim that Document 5-1 should be deemed withdrawn together with the statement of opinion, and that Jingkai Company's submission of Document 5-1 during the oral hearing exceeded the statutory evidentiary period, lacks factual and legal basis. This court does not support it.

(2) The issue regarding the submission of the translation of Document 5-1

Cao Zhongquan argued that the translation of Document 5-1 submitted by Jingkai Company on December 29, 2008, was 12 pages, but the Patent Reexamination Board used a modified 7-page translation, which contained multiple revisions and was inaccurate. This court holds that the cited document in this case is Document 5-1 itself, not its translation. Cao Zhongquan raised no objection to the authenticity of Document 5-1. Therefore, the content disclosed in Document 5-1 is objective and does not change due to any change in the translation. The differences between the two translations pointed out by Cao Zhongquan are merely differences in wording and have no effect on the substantive content. Moreover, the oral hearing record of the Patent Reexamination Board indicates that the translation of Document 5-1 used by both parties during the oral hearing was the 7-page translation, and Cao Zhongquan explicitly stated that he had no objection to the accuracy of that translation and made his remarks based on the 7-page translation. Therefore, it was not improper for the Patent Reexamination Board to describe the content disclosed in Document 5-1 based on the 7-page translation.

(3) Regarding the inventiveness of this patent

Inventiveness is an essential characteristic of inventions and creations, representing the level of innovation required for an invention or creation compared to the prior art. The requirement for inventiveness of utility models under the Chinese Patent Law is that compared with the prior art before the filing date, the utility model has substantive features and represents progress. When evaluating whether an invention or creation possesses inventiveness, not only the technical solution itself should be considered, but also the technical field to which the invention or creation belongs, the technical problem it solves, and the technical effects it produces, taking them as a whole. That is, a comprehensive determination should be made from the perspectives of the technical principles, technical conception, and technical effects of the invention or creation.

1. Regarding the technical field. Cao Zhongquan argued that this patent and Document 5-1 have different international classification numbers, and they are neither the same technical field nor similar or related technical fields, therefore Document 5-1 cannot be used as a cited document for evaluating the inventiveness of this patent. This court holds that the technical field is the specific technical field to which the claimed invention or utility model belongs or is applied, not a broader or adjacent technical field, nor the invention or creation itself. The technical field to which an invention or utility model belongs should be determined based on the content defined in the claims, generally in accordance with the subject matter of the patent, taking into account the technical functions and uses achieved by the technical solution. Document 5-1 discloses technical content relating to the lubrication of a winding machine lubrication system, while the technical solution of this patent aims to solve the oil retention and lubrication problem of the helical gear set in a cutting machine. Although the winding machine is a textile machine and the cutting machine is a garment machine, and they differ in application environment, the technical solutions of this patent and the cited document both relate to the lubrication of mechanical systems and belong to the same technical field. Therefore, the Patent Reexamination Board's use of Document 5-1 as a cited document for assessing the inventiveness of this patent was not improper.

2.  Regarding the technical features. The patent at issue is an oil retention device for a helical gear set in a cutting machine sharpening mechanism. According to the patent's claims and specification, to achieve its inventive purpose, the patent sets oil-retaining walls around the helical gear and the intermediate gear to retain splashed lubricating oil around the helical gear; and sets an arc-shaped cover plate at the transmission gear position outside the wall to prevent oil from being thrown out of the wall. From the technical features of the lubrication system disclosed in Exhibit 5-1, the technical problem actually solved and the technical effect produced are not the same as those of the patent at issue. In Exhibit 5-1, the lubrication system composed of oil slinger 160, gears 146, 150, guard 200 and baffle 206 primarily functions to obtain lubricating oil from the oil tank 162 and deliver the lubricating oil to the components requiring lubrication. The primary purpose of setting the direct forward portion 200A, the cylindrical portion 200B, the rear arc portion 200C of the guard 200 and the baffle 206 is to serve the above-mentioned technical functions. To this end, the guard 200 is provided with an oil inlet to obtain lubricating oil from the oil tank, and the baffle 206 is provided with an inlet/outlet 204 to receive the lubricating oil. Since the technical problem to be solved by the patent at issue differs from that of Exhibit 5-1, the technical effects achieved are also different. The technical effect achieved by the technical features of the patent at issue is to retain the lubricating oil around the gear without leakage, to achieve good gear lubrication and prevent the lubricating oil from contaminating the cloth; the technical effect achieved by the guard 200 and the baffle 206 is to deliver the lubricating oil outwards, rather than retaining it around the gear without leakage.

3.  Regarding technical inspiration. The main technical problem to be solved by the technical solution of the lubrication system disclosed in Exhibit 5-1 is to effectively deliver lubricating oil to lubricate the internal components of the winding machine, rather than preventing oil splashing to contaminate the cloth. For a person of ordinary skill in the art, upon seeing the technical solution disclosed in Exhibit 5-1, there is no motivation to improve the technical features of the guard 200 and the baffle 206 in the lubrication system and apply them to the cutting machine sharpening mechanism to solve the technical problem of preventing oil splashing and retaining the lubricating oil around the helical gear as required by the patent at issue. Therefore, Exhibit 5-1 does not provide a technical inspiration for a person of ordinary skill in the art to arrive at the technical solution and technical effect claimed in the patent at issue.

In summary, the technical solution claimed in claim 1 of the patent at issue is non-obvious with respect to the comparative document Exhibit 5-1, has substantive features and represents progress, and possesses the inventiveness required under Article 22, paragraph 3 of the Patent Law. Since claim 1 of the patent at issue is inventive, dependent claims 2 and 3 are also inventive. The judgments of the first and second instances, which found that the patent at issue lacked inventiveness relative to Exhibit 5-1 and thus affirmed Decision No. 13216 of the Patent Reexamination Board, applied the law incorrectly and should be corrected.

Pursuant to Article 54, paragraph (2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, when a people's court renders a judgment to revoke or partially revoke the specific administrative act under suit, it may also render a judgment ordering the defendant to make a new specific administrative act, but whether to order the defendant to make a new specific administrative act depends on the specific circumstances of the case. When a people's court reviews an invalidation request review decision of the Patent Reexamination Board, in cases where the Patent Reexamination Board considers the patent valid but the people's court considers it invalid, when rendering a judgment to revoke the decision under suit, the court should also order the Patent Reexamination Board to make a new decision. In cases where the Patent Reexamination Board considers the patent invalid, when the people's court renders a judgment to revoke the decision under suit, whether to also order the Patent Reexamination Board to make a new decision should be distinguished into the following two situations: if the Patent Reexamination Board has fully examined all the invalidation grounds and evidence raised by the invalidation requester, and the people's court considers the patent valid, there is no need to order the Patent Reexamination Board to make a new decision; if the Patent Reexamination Board has not fully examined all the invalidation grounds and evidence raised by the invalidation requester, and the invalidation decision based on some grounds and corresponding evidence cannot stand, the people's court should also order the Patent Reexamination Board to make a new decision on the other invalidation grounds and evidence raised by the invalidation requester. In this case, the invalidation grounds raised by Jingkai Company against the patent at issue before the Patent Reexamination Board were that claims 1, 2, and 3 of the patent at issue did not comply with Article 22, paragraphs 2 and 3, Article 26, paragraphs 3 and 4 of the Patent Law, and Article 20, paragraph 1 of the Implementing Regulations; claim 3 did not comply with Article 21, paragraph 3 of the Implementing Regulations. Jingkai Company also submitted multiple comparative documents, including Exhibit 5-1, to evaluate the novelty and inventiveness of the claimed patent. When making Decision No. 13216, the Patent Reexamination Board evaluated the claims of the patent at issue as lacking inventiveness based on Exhibit 5-1 and accordingly declared the patent wholly invalid, without commenting on the other invalidation grounds and evidence raised by Jingkai Company. In view of this, after this Court renders a judgment to revoke Decision No. 13216 made by the Patent Reexamination Board, the Patent Reexamination Board should make a new decision on the other invalidation grounds and evidence raised by Jingkai Company. Therefore, in accordance with Article 54, paragraph (2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 76, paragraph 1 and Article 78 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1.  Revoke the Administrative Judgment (2010) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 634 of the Beijing High People's Court and the Administrative Judgment (2009) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 1326 of the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court;

2.  Revoke Invalidation Request Review Decision No. 13216 of the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office;

3.  The Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office shall make a new decision on the other invalidation grounds and evidence raised by Shanghai Jingkai Garment Machinery Co., Ltd. against Utility Model Patent No. 200520014575.5 owned by Cao Zhongquan.

The first and second instance case acceptance fees of RMB 100 each, totaling RMB 200, shall be borne by the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office (to be paid within seven days from the date this judgment takes effect).

This judgment is final.
